title: Jellyroll-wound memory ribbon: battery winding replaces tier deposition
idea: Borrowing the lithium-ion jellyroll, fabricate a long released ribbon (thin polyimide on a sacrificial carrier) carrying one tier of low-temperature thin-film transistors and planar MIM capacitors, then wind it on a mandrel so every turn becomes a tier. Tier-to-tier and tier-to-logic contacts run through edge tabs exactly like battery current collectors, landing on a radial bus bonded to the CMOS base.
why: 3D tier count and capital (facts 2, 4): one patterning pass per ribbon yields 100+ effective tiers by winding instead of 100 deposition/etch cycles; claims ~10x lower capex per tier, accepting low per-tier density.

title: Fresnel capacitor: nested shallow shells replace one tall pillar
idea: As a Fresnel lens collapses a thick lens into concentric rings, collapse a 75:1 pillar into 3-4 concentric electrode shells nested in one cell footprint: alternate ALD of TiN, high-k and a sacrificial spacer inside a single ~20:1 hole, then selectively strip the spacers so both faces of every shell become capacitor area.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): roughly the area of a 75:1 pillar at AR ~20, cutting the hardest etch depth 3-4x and pillar leaning; claims 5 fF at a fraction of the high-AR etch cost.

title: Croissant lamination: tier doubling by repeated wafer fold-and-bond
idea: Like laminated dough that doubles its layers with every fold, grow an 8-tier Si/SiGe superlattice once, then bond the wafer face-to-face onto a copy of itself, Smart-Cut the donor and repeat, so four bond cycles give 128 tiers. No single epitaxy run ever exceeds the SiGe strain-relaxation limit, and each tier keeps single-crystal quality for the lateral transistor.
why: No manufacturable 3D DRAM cell (fact 2): the 26+ tier break-even stalls on strain and defects in thick superlattices; exponential tier count with log2 bonding steps claims >100 tiers in ~4-5 bonds.

title: Sky-lobby decoder decks: in-stack tier decoders fed by express vias
idea: Skyscrapers use express elevators to sky lobbies, then local cars; build a 128-tier 3D DRAM as 8 decks of 16 tiers, each deck capped by a thin-film decoder tier that receives a 4-bit tier address over a few express vias and fans out locally to its 16 wordline planes through a short mini-staircase.
why: 3D staircase and periphery (facts 2, 7): wires from the CMOS base drop from one per tier to ~log2 per deck, shrinking the staircase/contact region ~4-8x and letting tier count rise without periphery growth.

title: Back-contact solar layout: bitlines moved to the wafer backside
idea: Interdigitated-back-contact solar cells free the front surface by putting all metal behind; do the same for vertical-channel DRAM: after front-side capacitors are built, bond to a carrier, thin to the channel bottoms and form buried bitlines from the backside, so the front is 100% capacitor landing at true 4F2.
why: Litho-bound cell layout (fact 4): removes bitline contacts and shields that block 4F2 vertical-channel cells; claims ~33% less area per bit than 6F2 at the same F, a node of gain without extra EUV.

title: Shingled mushroom capacitors: SMR-style overlap of two height tiers
idea: Like shingled magnetic recording overlapping tracks, build capacitors in two interleaved heights: even cells get a short pillar topped by a wide mushroom electrode at level 1, odd cells a taller pillar whose cap sits at level 2, so every cap overhangs its neighbours' footprint.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): ~1.8x electrode area per footprint at unchanged aspect ratio, giving either ~9 fF or a cell shrink at constant Cs.

title: Fiber-draw nanocapillary scaffold grown on a draw tower, not etched
idea: Use the optical-fiber draw tower: stack a centimetre preform of glass rods with soluble cores, draw it down ~10,000x into a fused bundle with ~40 nm channels and >1000:1 aspect ratio, slice 3 um wafers, bond them onto the transistor wafer, and ALD electrodes plus high-k into the channels to form the capacitor forest.
why: Capacitor wall and etch capital (facts 1, 4): AR far beyond the 115 target with zero deep plasma etch; replaces cryogenic high-AR etch tools with draw towers costing a few $M.

title: MicroLED mass transfer of known-good DRAM micro-tiles
idea: Adopt microLED display mass transfer: make DRAM arrays as 200 um micro-tiles on a dense array wafer, test and map them, then stamp-transfer only good tiles, thousands per stroke, onto a periphery/logic wafer with hybrid-bond landing pads, assembling dies from perfect tiles.
why: Yield and HBM tax (fact 6): tile-level known-good assembly recovers the 20-30% stack yield loss and lets the array wafer run a stripped-down process; claims ~25% lower cost per bit.

title: Termite-mound thermosiphon chimneys through the DRAM stack
idea: Termite mounds cool themselves with passive convection chimneys; etch a sparse grid of sealed ~20 um chimneys through a 16-24 high bonded DRAM stack, partly filled with a dielectric working fluid that boils near the hot logic tier and condenses at the lid, pumping heat with no pump.
why: Thermal ceiling on stack height and refresh (facts 3, 6): retention roughly halves per 10 C, so keeping upper tiers ~15 C cooler cuts refresh ~2-3x and allows ~1.5x more tiers per stack within the thermal budget.

title: Self-ordering anodic pore lattice sets the cell pitch litho-free
idea: Borrow anodized-aluminium battery and supercapacitor electrodes: anodize a deposited Al film over a coarse seed pattern (every 4th site) so it self-organizes into a hexagonal pore lattice at ~30 nm pitch and AR >100, then use the same pores as templates for both vertical-channel access transistors and capacitors in one self-aligned lattice.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4) and capacitor AR (fact 1): bottom-up hexagonal 4F2-equivalent array with only coarse lithography; claims elimination of 2-3 EUV layers and AR >100 at no etch cost.

title: Woven wordlines zig-zag between tier pairs like weft threads
idea: Treat wordlines as weft threads: each lateral wordline hops between tier k and k+1 every 32 cells through short vias while its partner runs in the opposite phase, so a raised wordline opens a checkerboard row spanning both tiers. Address logic maps it as one logical row, so one staircase contact serves two tiers and systematic tier-thickness variation averages out.
why: 3D staircase area and tier variability (facts 2, 7): halves staircase contacts and their decoder footprint; claims ~2x shorter staircase region and a tighter access-transistor Vt distribution.

title: Lift-slab tier manufacturing across idle mature fabs
idea: Like lift-slab construction where floors are cast on the ground and jacked into place, run each tier of a bonded 3D DRAM stack as a simple array-only wafer (1-2 critical layers) in under-used U.S. 65-28 nm fabs, then ship tier wafers to one bonding hub that hybrid-bonds and thins them into 8-16 tier stacks.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital (fact 4, resources): reuses depreciated fabs instead of $15B greenfield; claims U.S. DRAM capacity without EUV at ~3-4x lower capex per wafer-tier.

title: ISO-container memory tile: an open hybrid-bond array standard
idea: Standardize a memory container: a 1 Gb array tile with fixed footprint, fixed hybrid-bond pad map (sense-amp interface, power, test) and fixed timing protocol, so any maker's array tile bonds onto any vendor's base die, as ISO containers did for shipping.
why: Capital intensity and supply diversity (facts 4, 6): new array makers (oxide, 3D, legacy fabs) can enter without building periphery and I/O; claims faster capacity ramp and commodity tile pricing.

title: CDO tranching: retention-binned die pools before stacking
idea: Treat dies like loan pools: measure each array die's retention tail and speed at wafer sort, sort into tranches and build stacks only from matching tranches (senior tranche to HBM with relaxed refresh, junior to consumer DRAM), instead of stacking randomly and binning the stack by its worst die.
why: HBM yield (fact 6) and refresh (fact 3): stacks stop inheriting the worst die; claims 10-15% more sellable stacks and a premium tier with 2x refresh interval.

title: Basement-and-rooftop sandwich: periphery split across two bonded wafers
idea: Copy buildings that put plant rooms in the basement and on the roof: a three-wafer stack with row decoders and wordline drivers bonded below the array wafer and sense amplifiers plus column logic bonded above it, each at line pitch, leaving the middle array wafer 100% cells.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): array efficiency rises toward ~90%; claims ~1.7x bits per array-wafer area with periphery on cheaper logic nodes.

title: Wavelength-addressed tiers: color-coded phototransistor tier select
idea: Like wavelength-division multiplexing in fibre, give each tier's select transistors a different absorber bandgap (graded SiGe or tuned quantum dots) and light the stack through an in-plane waveguide grid at one wavelength, so only that tier's selectors turn on and no staircase or per-tier decoder is needed.
why: 3D staircase and periphery (facts 2, 7): staircase area goes to zero for 16-32 tiers and tier decoding moves off-die into a tunable laser.

title: Column-inversion storage cancels bitline coupling, like LCD panels
idea: LCD drivers alternate pixel polarity column by column to cancel crosstalk; store data in alternating true/complement polarity on adjacent bitlines and flip the pattern each row, so neighbour-swing coupling arrives common-mode at each sense amp and cancels, allowing tighter vertical-bitline pitch without shield lines.
why: Density in 3D arrays and signal margin (facts 1, 2): removes shield lines (~20-30% of bitline pitch) and recovers ~30% signal; claims ~1.25x density.

title: Corrugated-board substrate: one array film over V-groove relief
idea: Like corrugated cardboard folding a flat sheet into a high-area core, KOH-etch Si(100) into 54.7-degree V-grooves at ~200 nm pitch and build a thin-film transistor-capacitor array conformally on both groove faces with tilted implants and spacer patterning, packing ~1.7x more planar-processed cells per footprint.
why: Density without tier stacking (fact 4): ~1.7x area from one cheap wet etch while reusing planar steps, sidestepping the 26-tier break-even.

title: Kinematic-coupling self-alignment for cheap fine-pitch die stacking
idea: Use precision-optics kinematic mounts (three balls in three V-grooves): etch inverted pyramids into the base die and tapered posts on each tier die so dies settle into sub-50 nm registration by geometry during fluid-assisted placement, letting fast coarse pick-and-place feed fine-pitch hybrid bonding.
why: Stacking capital and throughput (facts 4, 6): replaces $10M-class high-precision die-to-wafer bonders with fast placement plus self-alignment; claims 5-10x bonding throughput.

title: Helical parking-ramp tier contacts instead of a staircase
idea: Like a spiral parking ramp reaching every level without stairs, deposit the tier stack conformally over a pre-etched helical ramp in a ring trench; after one planarization every tier surfaces at a different angular position on a flat ring, contacted by a single litho of radial vias.
why: 3D staircase cost and area (facts 2, 7): N trim-etch cycles become one ramp etch plus CMP; claims ~5x smaller contact region for 64+ tiers.

title: Mobile-shelving sense amps: one aisle serves eight stacked mats
idea: Like compact library shelving that opens one aisle at a time, put one sense-amp stripe at the base of eight vertically bonded subarrays sharing a vertical bitline through isolation switches, so only the opened subarray connects to the amplifiers at a time.
why: Periphery ~49% (fact 7): sense-amp area amortized 8x instead of today's 2x shared-SA; claims ~25-30% smaller die.

title: Decal capacitors: high-temperature forest transferred onto transistors
idea: Like a water-slide decal, build the capacitor forest on a donor wafer at 600-800 C, allowing crystalline rutile TiO2 or SrTiO3 (k ~80-150), then bond it upside-down onto a finished access-transistor wafer and remove the donor, so the dielectric never meets the transistor's thermal limit.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): k ~100 directly meets the k ~70 requirement; claims 2x Cs at half the aspect ratio (AR ~35).

title: Cell-to-pack memory: unsingulated DRAM wafers bonded onto compute wafers
idea: Like EV cell-to-pack removing the module layer, skip die singulation, packages and DIMMs: wafer-bond whole yield-mapped DRAM wafers (with spare-tile rerouting) onto whole compute wafers so memory meets compute through millions of bonds at full wafer scale.
why: HBM TSV tax and data movement (facts 5, 6): removes TSVs, interposer and package; claims ~3x area efficiency vs HBM and ~100 TB/s per wafer pair.

title: Hotel-keycard micro-rows: coincident gating opens only 64 bits
idea: Like a keycard that opens one room instead of the whole floor, give each 3D DRAM cell a series pair of access gates, the tier wordline plus a vertical column-group select, so an activation opens only the 64 cells at the intersection rather than an 8 Kb page, and only those bitlines swing and restore.
why: Destructive read and overfetch (fact 8): 128x overfetch falls to ~1x, so activate-plus-restore energy per useful bit claims >10x lower (5.9 pJ toward <0.5 pJ).

title: Darkroom development: pillar-foot gain transistor reads a 0.5 fF cell
idea: Like a latent photographic image amplified by development, store only ~0.5 fF per 3D cell and put one thin-film gain transistor at the foot of every 16-cell vertical local bitline; the cell perturbs only ~1 fF of local line and the gain device converts it into current on a 100 mV-swing global line.
why: Energy per access and capacitor wall (facts 1, 8, 10): switched capacitance per read falls from ~85 fF at 1 V to a few fF plus a low-swing global line; claims ~10x lower read energy.

title: RV 12-volt rule: short pillars let the array run at 0.35 V
idea: Low-voltage DC works in RVs because the runs are short; build vertical-bitline mats with 32-cell bitlines (Cb ~1.5 fF), giving a charge-transfer ratio near 0.6 that supports sensing at VARY 0.35 V with a ~100 mV signal, with sense amps in a bonded low-voltage logic wafer.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): V from 1.0 to 0.35 V gives ~8x on CV2 and Cb is ~50x smaller than planar bitlines; claims >10x lower array energy per access.

title: Pendulum wordline planes: resonant LC drive recycles plate charge
idea: Like a pendulum clock trading kinetic for potential energy, make the large horizontal wordline plates of a 3D array the capacitor of an LC tank with an interposer spiral inductor, swinging the selected plate sinusoidally to VPP and back so ~85% of its charge returns to the inductor instead of ground.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): ~3 V wordline CV2 dominates plate-wordline 3D DRAM; claims 5-10x lower wordline energy per activation.

title: Canal-lock water-saving basins for bitline precharge
idea: German canal locks store emptied water in side basins at intermediate heights and reuse it to refill; give each mat 8 on-pitch reservoir capacitors at VDD/8 steps so bitlines discharging after a row closes dump charge stepwise into the basins and the next subarray's bitlines refill from them, taking only the final step from the supply.
why: Bitline CV2 (facts 8, 10): stepwise charging with N basins cuts supply energy roughly N-fold; claims ~6-8x lower bitline energy per access.

title: Fifteen-minute city: a private DRAM tile bonded over every core
idea: Urbanists keep essentials within a short walk; hybrid-bond at 1 um pitch a 64 MB 3D DRAM tile directly above each compute-core cluster so its data travels under 100 um vertically through ~10k bonds with 0.3 V signalling, with no PHY, SerDes or interposer.
why: Data movement (fact 5): HBM 3-4 pJ/bit and DDR5 10-20 pJ/bit vs ~0.05-0.1 pJ/bit transport; claims >10x lower energy per delivered bit.

title: Pantry kitchen: per-mat reduction engines in a bonded logic tier
idea: Cook where the food is stored: a logic tier bonded beneath each 3D DRAM mat carries one bit-serial adder/comparator per 64 sense amps, so dot-products, top-k and sums over a row finish in place and only the reduced result, 1/64 of the bits, leaves the mat.
why: Data movement and overfetch (facts 5, 8): bits moved per useful result drop ~64x; claims 10-30x lower energy per AI access such as attention scoring.

title: Freight consolidation hub: base die sorts requests by row
idea: Like a cross-dock that fills containers before shipping, a 32 MB SRAM queue in the HBM/3D base die holds ~50k pending requests, radix-sorts them by row in hardware and fires an activation only when 32+ lines for that row are waiting or a deadline expires.
why: Activation amortization (fact 8): each activation serves 32-64 useful lines instead of 1-2 for random traffic; claims ~10x lower energy per access on latency-tolerant AI and graph workloads.

title: Light-switch air gap: NEMS relay access device in BEOL tiers
idea: A wall switch draws nothing when off because of its air gap; make each 3D cell's access device a laterally actuated ~10 nm-gap TiN/Ru NEMS relay built at BEOL temperatures, whose near-zero off-current lets the capacitor shrink to ~0.3 fF (signal-limited, not retention-limited) and removes refresh.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3): refresh's ~46 fJ/bit disappears and cell plus local-line charge drops ~10x; claims ~10x lower energy per access if contact endurance holds.

title: E-paper bistability: antiferroelectric cell read nondestructively by capacitance
idea: Like e-paper holding an image unpowered, use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor with asymmetric electrodes whose built-in bias keeps it stable in either the AFE or field-induced FE phase, then read with a 50 mV AC probe of differential capacitance (the phases differ ~2x), disturbing neither state, so no restore and no refresh.
why: Destructive read and refresh (facts 3, 8): no full-swing restore, no refresh; claims >10x lower read energy (50 mV probe vs ~1 V restore).

title: Fire-brigade bucket chain: CCD charge transfer to a tiny sense node
idea: Like a bucket brigade passing water hand to hand, read a vertical 16-cell string CCD-style: 4-phase 0.5 V transfer gates clock the selected cell's charge along a buried channel to a ~0.3 fF floating diffusion with a source follower and correlated double sampling, and reverse clocking writes it back.
why: Energy per access (facts 8, 10): no bitline swing at all, only low-voltage transfer gates and a tiny high-gain node; claims >10x lower read energy and supports ~0.2 fF cells.

title: Drip irrigation: ground-precharged bitlines with sparsity-maximizing encoding
idea: Water only the plants that need it: precharge bitlines to 0 V instead of VDD/2 and store each 64-bit word in whichever polarity has fewer ones (plus a flag bit), paired with zero-skewed tensor formats, so only bitlines that read a 1 draw charge.
why: Bitline energy proportional to ones (facts 8, 10): with ReLU/quantized tensors at 5-15% ones after encoding, claims 5-10x lower bitline energy per access.

title: Video P-frames: delta bitlines swing only when data changes
idea: Video codecs send only what changed between frames; skip bitline equalization between successive activations in a subarray and sense each new row against the bitline's previous value with a dummy-cell reference, so a bitline toggles only where the new row differs, while the controller orders correlated rows back to back.
why: Bitline energy proportional to Hamming distance (fact 8): for streaming tensors and KV pages with ~10% bit toggles, claims up to ~10x lower bitline energy.

title: Gearbox gate: negative-capacitance access transistor runs 0.8 V wordlines
idea: Like a gearbox multiplying torque, add a thin ferroelectric negative-capacitance layer matched to the access-transistor gate so the channel potential swings ~3x the wordline swing; drive wordlines 0-0.8 V while keeping the 13 fA off-state and drop the VPP charge pump.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): wordline CV2 scales by (0.8/3)^2 ~ 1/14, plus ~3x pump inefficiency removed; claims >10x lower wordline energy.

title: Progressive-JPEG bit-plane tiers: fetch only the precision needed
idea: Progressive JPEG sends coarse bits first; store each tensor element's bits across separate 3D tiers (MSB plane, next plane, and so on) so a pass needing 4-bit precision activates 4 of 16 bit-plane rows, and MSB-plane zeros mask whole lower-plane fetches.
why: Precision overfetch (facts 5, 8): bits activated and moved per useful value drop 4x, toward ~10x with MSB-gated skipping; claims ~10x lower energy per AI access.

title: Fiber-to-the-mat: photonic waveguide layer replaces TSV I/O
idea: Like fibre-to-the-home replacing copper last miles, put a silicon-nitride waveguide layer in the 3D DRAM base die with micro-ring modulators per mat cluster, carrying data at ~30 fJ/bit straight from local datalines to an off-stack optical link with no global copper datalines, TSV drivers or SerDes.
why: Data movement (facts 5, 6): ~2-3 pJ/bit of global dataline, TSV and PHY energy replaced by ~0.1-0.2 pJ/bit optical path; claims ~10x lower energy per bit delivered.

title: Post-it tier: tiny 1 ms-retention cells for transient data
idea: A Post-it is cheap because it need not last; dedicate a 3D tier to 0.5 fF cells with ~1 ms retention on short bitlines for data whose lifetime is shorter than that (activations, in-flight KV, gradients), placed there by the compiler and never refreshed.
why: Capacitor wall, refresh and access energy (facts 1, 3, 8): ~10x smaller Cs and shorter lines cut switched charge ~10x with zero refresh; claims ~10x lower energy per access for transient traffic.

title: Noise-cancelling headphones: replica-bitline subtraction enables tiny signals
idea: Like ANC headphones playing anti-noise, give every 8 bitlines a cell-less replica bitline that sees the same wordline kick and neighbour coupling; the sense amp subtracts it in the charge domain, so 30 mV signals become reliable and VARY drops to ~0.4 V.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): 1.0 to 0.4 V gives ~6x on CV2, and the smaller required signal allows ~1.5x smaller Cs; claims ~8-10x lower array energy.

title: Garage-door spring: tier back-plate bias lowers wordline swing
idea: A torsion spring carries most of a garage door's weight; give the lateral access transistors of each 3D tier a shared back-gate plate held at a retention-safe negative bias, and switch only the tier being served to a Vt-lowering bias for a batch of accesses, so front wordlines need only a ~0.9 V swing.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): wordline energy ~ V2 drops ~11x from 3 V to 0.9 V; plate switching is amortized over hundreds of accesses per tier dwell.

title: Radio broadcast reads: one activation multicast to many consumers
idea: One transmitter serves a whole city; in a 3D DRAM-on-logic stack, activate a row of shared weights once and multicast it over a base-die broadcast bus to all 16-64 compute tiles subscribed to that row address in the same step (batched or tensor-parallel inference).
why: Activation and movement energy (facts 5, 8): one access serves N consumers; claims 10-60x lower energy per delivered weight in batched inference.

title: Tesla-valve diode cells: crosspoint 1D1C array without wordline gates
idea: A Tesla valve rectifies flow with no moving parts; build a crosspoint 3D array where each capacitor is reached through a wide-bandgap Ga2O3/NiO heterojunction thin-film diode, selected by coincidence of a 1.2 V row-plate pulse and a bitline offset, removing the 3 V gated wordline and the access transistor.
why: Voltage floor and density (facts 2, 10): no VPP wordline and 4F2 crosspoint stacking in BEOL; claims ~10x lower select energy, provided diode reverse leakage stays below ~1 fA.

title: Photomultiplier read: avalanche gain junction under each pillar
idea: Like a photomultiplier or SPAD turning one photon into a pulse, place a quenched avalanche junction at the foot of each vertical bitline biased just below breakdown; a 0.1 fF cell's few hundred electrons trigger ~100x multiplication, then a passive quench resets it, so cells and lines stay tiny.
why: Capacitor wall and access energy (facts 1, 8): Cs drops ~50x and the local line stays a few fF; claims >10x lower energy per read if avalanche statistics and dark counts are tamed.

title: Thermos flask: sealed vacuum gaps around vertical bitlines
idea: Like a vacuum flask, after the 3D stack is built, selectively remove a sacrificial carbon or SiGe interlayer between vertical bitlines and wordline plates and pinch it shut with a non-conformal cap, replacing k ~4 fill with vacuum.
why: Bitline capacitance and voltage floor (facts 8, 10): Cb ~3x lower lets Cs shrink 3x at the same transfer ratio, and lower coupling allows VARY ~0.6 V; claims ~3x x ~3x = ~9-10x lower energy per access.
